body.heading: Repetition is the secret ingredient
paragraphs: School made friends for us by locking us in the same rooms for years. Adulthood removes the machinery, so we must supply it ourselves: the same class, club, shift, or dog-walking hour, again and again. Familiarity does most of the work — you just have to keep showing up.
Choose something you would enjoy even if no friendship came of it. That way the experiment cannot fail.

body.heading: Be the one who suggests
paragraphs: Almost everyone is waiting to be invited, which means the person who suggests the coffee holds unusual power. “A few of us are trying the new bakery on Saturday — come if you like” is low-pressure for them and low-risk for you.
Expect a success rate, not a success story. Some invitations will land flat; that is arithmetic, not rejection. The people who build wide circles simply ask more often.

body.heading: Grow it in small deposits
paragraphs: New adult friendships grow through small, reliable deposits: remembering the exam date, sending the article they would like, turning up when you said you would. Grand gestures are not required and can even alarm a new acquaintance.
Give it months. The friendships that look effortless from outside are usually just old, and yours are simply young.

takeaway: Show up repeatedly, be the one who suggests, and let small deposits do the compounding.
